bull_bear.body: The company's credit rating update may have implications for its future business operations and financial position.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- One of the few companies in India providing end-to-end services in the upstream oil segment across the value chain, from seismic data acquisition and data analysis to building oil & gas facilities and undertaking O&M of production facilities
- 34 years of experience in the industry, with a 31-year legacy in seismology
- Asset-light model focused on technical expertise and end-to-end project execution, with limited equipment ownership
- Long-duration recurring O&M contracts that provide stable revenues and enhance earnings visibility
- Long-standing relationships with leading energy companies and a proven record of successful project delivery
- Large order book providing multi-year revenue visibility, with over 500 employees and 50+ projects successfully completed
- International platform across the Middle East and Southeast Asia following the Kuiper Group acquisition
- Net zero-debt position on a standalone basis
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive intensity in seismic and integrated energy services — The growing number of seismic and integrated energy services providers may affect the Company's ability to secure new contracts. The Company states it maintains a competitive edge through strategic pricing, long-term client relationships and a proven record of successful project delivery. (MD&A 'Principal Risks and Mitigation Measures' — this table was routed to the strategy_outlook bundle rather than to this risks bundle, but is from the same annual report.)
- Environmental compliance exposure in coal operations — Non-compliance with environmental standards could damage the Company's reputation and reduce long-term demand for coal, potentially leading to lower coal prices. The Company has implemented a comprehensive Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) policy integrating environmental safeguards across its coal operations. (MD&A 'Principal Risks and Mitigation Measures', routed to the strategy_outlook bundle.)
- Geopolitical exposure in West Asia affecting the international business — Management explicitly flags that developments in West Asia remain a key variable to monitor, given their bearing on crude and LNG prices, shipping costs and the broader operating environment for energy services companies with an international footprint. The escalation of conflict in early 2026 disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and drove Brent from around USD 61 per barrel to a peak near USD 118 per barrel. With the Kuiper acquisition, a material part of the business now sits in the Middle East. (MD&A, routed to the strategy_outlook bundle.)
- Crude price volatility and structurally decelerating global oil demand — Prices have remained volatile, and global oil demand growth continued its structural deceleration, rising just 0.7% in 2025, with the IEA projecting an outright decline in demand for 2026. Global energy investment is increasingly directed toward renewables, grids, storage and low-emissions technologies rather than oil, gas and coal, which bears on long-run demand for upstream services. (MD&A, routed to the strategy_outlook bundle.)
- Execution and integration risk on transformative M&A — The Company is simultaneously integrating the newly acquired Kuiper Group, consolidated only from September 01, 2025, and pursuing the merger of its parent Oilmax Energy Private Limited, which remains subject to NCLT Mumbai hearing and final disposal and to regulatory clearances. Expected synergies, margin expansion and the scale-up to approximately USD 100 Million of Kuiper revenue depend on integration proceeding as planned.
- Customer and contract concentration in a project-driven order book — Revenue visibility rests on a standalone order book of approximately Rs 1,750 Crores concentrated in a small number of large contracts, with counterparties including Vedanta, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited, ONGC and Oil India. The award, deferral or loss of any single large contract materially affects the growth path.
- Project execution disruption from weather and site conditions — Management notes that extended monsoon conditions affected execution across certain projects during the first half of the year, requiring the teams to respond with agility and discipline to maintain project momentum — an ongoing structural exposure for a site-based EPC and material-handling business.
- Governance and regulatory compliance lapses flagged by the Secretarial Auditor — The Secretarial Auditor noted three observations: an analyst-meet intimation given at short notice without the required explanation, XBRL intimations for the May 16, 2025 Board Meeting outcome and the statutory auditor appointment filed with delay, and a postal-ballot remote e-voting window kept open beyond thirty days. Management responded that these were inadvertent and gave assurances of future adherence. Separately, the statutory auditors changed during the year, with Walker Chandiok & Co. resigning on completion of their second term and SGCO & Co. LLP appointed in their place.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Combines asset-light technical capabilities with owned energy assets and infrastructure to create an 'Integrated Energy Platform', offering one-stop upstream solutions across Exploration, Development, Production and Abandonment.
- O&G Services Spectrum covers end-to-end services from seismic surveys to turnkey O&M and production enhancement; Mineral Services span bulk material handling, mining and mineral processing.
- Well-diversified global customer relationships across Oil & Gas and Mining, reducing dependency on any single customer or geography; Oilmax-Asian and Kuiper give presence across India, the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Policy Tailwinds] Government programs cited as growth drivers: Samudra Manthan (INR 84,084 crore upfront Govt. capex to explore deep offshore), ORDA Act 2025 (single petroleum lease simplifying upstream approvals), Critical Minerals Mission, recently concluded DSF-IV auction/CBM round, and rising E&P outsourcing via Production Enhancement Contracts.
- [Leadership] Board and management team drawn from leading global MNCs and NOCs, with centralised HSE, project controls, supply chain and regulatory governance cited as a differentiator for single-point accountability and faster decision-making.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Asian Energy is a service provider to the energy and mineral sectors offering end-to-end services across the value chain, including seismic surveys and geophysical data acquisition, integrated field development, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC), operations and maintenance (O&M) and enhanced oil recovery. The business is anchored in two complementary verticals: Integrated Oil & Gas Services, which supports upstream clients through the asset lifecycle, and Mineral Services, which delivers coal handling plants, bulk material handling systems and related engineering and execution solutions. Following the acquisition of Kuiper Group, the Company also provides integrated human resources, technical staffing and recruitment solutions to the energy industry internationally.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Integrated Oil & Gas Services:** Seismic surveys, Geological studies, Exploratory & appraisal wells, Subsurface data interpretation, EPC and facility construction, Well drilling & testing, Commissioning & installation, Turnkey contract execution, Onshore/offshore O&M, Production enhancement services, Enhanced oil recovery
- **Mineral Services:** Coal handling plants (CHPs), Bulk material handling systems, Coal & material handling engineering and execution
- **Global Manpower & HR Solutions:** Integrated HR resourcing, EPCI, drilling and O&G staffing

outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body:
- Shift steadily from a project-based execution model to one driven by long-duration contracts, providing greater revenue visibility and improving earnings quality
- Maintain an asset-light business model focused on technical expertise and end-to-end project execution, with limited equipment ownership
- Transition from a project-execution services provider toward an integrated energy platform spanning exploration, development, production, operations and maintenance, and international manpower solutions
- Complete the proposed merger of Oilmax Energy Private Limited with the Company to combine upstream asset ownership with proven execution capabilities
- Integrate and scale up Kuiper Group to deepen the international presence across the Middle East and Southeast Asia and strengthen the recurring O&M business
- Grow the Mineral Services vertical beyond coal handling into wider material handling infrastructure, supported by increasing investments in mining, bulk commodities and critical minerals
- Pursue larger integrated field development contracts as the industry shifts toward integrated models that bring multiple technical capabilities under a single execution framework
- Shift the Kuiper business mix toward higher-value technical services to drive margin expansion alongside synergies and operational efficiencies
- Bid for new upstream acreage, having submitted bids for three contract areas under Discovered Small Field Bid Round-4
- Focus on disciplined execution, prudent capital allocation, technological innovation and operational excellence
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Asian Energy's expansion during 2025-26 was driven by acquisition and contract wins rather than by plant capex. The Company acquired a 100% equity stake in Kuiper Group, UAE, from Gulf Capital through its wholly owned subsidiary Asian Oilfield & Energy Services DMCC ('ADMCC') for a cash consideration of USD 9.25 Million, giving immediate access to energy markets across the Middle East and Southeast Asia; Kuiper Group consolidated into the Company's financials from September 01, 2025. In parallel, the Company announced the proposed merger of its parent Oilmax Energy Private Limited with itself, which shareholders approved at meetings held on June 11 and June 12, 2026 and which is expected to complete by September or October 2026 subject to regulatory clearances; the merger would add five oil & gas blocks including one CBM asset, approximately 70 Million barrels of hydrocarbon reserves and current production of about 2,500 BOPD targeted to reach about 10,000 BOPD by 2028-29/2029-30. On execution, the Company secured an integrated field management contract with Vedanta Resources and the Lakhanpur coal handling plant project from Mahanadi Coalfields Limited, the largest CHP contract in its history, alongside the Suvali O&M and Gevra CHP contracts. At its Indrora block in Gujarat the NM-01 well began producing approximately 100 barrels of oil per day, with a further well NM-02 under testing and a field development plan under implementation targeting block-level production of approximately 1,000 barrels of oil per day by 2026-27; a newly discovered Mewad field is also earmarked for ramp-up. The Company describes its model as asset-light, focused on technical expertise and end-to-end project execution with limited equipment ownership, and reported that there are no capital commitments as on the respective reporting periods.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's energy security agenda, targeting a USD 100 Billion commitment to oil & gas investment by 2030, is expected to continue driving exploration and production activity, field redevelopment and integrated outsourcing of upstream operations
- Continued government focus on scientific exploration under HELP, OALP and DSF frameworks is expected to sustain demand for seismic and allied services
- The coal sector's production targets and asset monetization plans point to continued mineral infrastructure and material handling opportunities
- Growing industry preference for integrated field development models, which management believes will increasingly become the preferred operating model for upstream companies seeking greater productivity, operational efficiency and optimized lifecycle costs
- Long-term O&M contracts provide stable revenues, enhance earnings visibility and strengthen customer relationships
- India's hydrocarbon consumption continued to expand, with crude oil demand projected close to 6 Million barrels per day for 2026, while domestic crude production remained broadly range-bound, keeping import dependency elevated
- The Union Budget for 2026-27 allocated Rs 30,443 Crores to the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas and raised overall capital expenditure to Rs 12.2 Lakh Crores, or 4.4% of GDP, its highest share in a decade
- Domestic coal production is on track to approach a record 1.15 Billion tonnes in 2025-26 with the government targeting 1.31 Billion tonnes for 2026-27, alongside a coal asset monetization target of Rs 35,000 Crores
- Developments in West Asia remain a key variable to monitor, given their bearing on crude and LNG prices, shipping costs and the broader operating environment for energy services companies with an international footprint
- Kuiper integration is expected to unlock meaningful operational synergies, with margin upside from synergies, efficiencies and a shift to higher-value technical services
- The proposed Oilmax merger is expected to strengthen the balance sheet, improve capital allocation, enhance operational efficiency and create a more diversified business with balanced recurring and project-based revenue streams
- The Reserve Bank of India has projected growth of 6.6% for 2026-27, with inflation expected to firm to around 5.1% amid continuing global uncertainty, crude price volatility and currency pressures
- The Company's standalone order book stood at approximately Rs 1,750 Crores as of March 31, 2026, with a split of approximately 68% coming from oil & gas services verticals and approximately 32% from mineral services, providing revenue visibility for the coming years
- Integrated Oil & Gas Services formed around 68% of the total order book of approximately Rs 1,750 Crores, providing strong multi-year revenue visibility
- Mineral Services represented approximately 32% of the order book, equivalent to over Rs 566 Crores, providing a strong platform for future growth
- The Company secured two substantial new contracts during the year: an integrated field management contract with Vedanta Resources, and the Lakhanpur coal handling plant project awarded by Mahanadi Coalfields Limited, the largest CHP contract in the Company's history
- The Company submitted bids for three contract areas under Discovered Small Field Bid Round-4, and has been placed L1 in one additional coal handling plant tender
- The Kuiper acquisition provides revenue visibility of approximately USD 60-65 Million per annum through existing contracts and master service agreements
- A large bid pipeline in the services business provides a strong base for the next 2-3 years

deepdive.thesis: Asian Energy Services Ltd has received a credit rating update from Crisil Ratings Limited, with an enhanced rated amount and a maintained 'Watch Developing' rating, indicating a developing implication on the company's long-term and short-term banking facilities. The company's energy services operations are crucial in the current energy landscape. The rating update reflects the company's financial position and outlook.

open.item: The Board has recommended a dividend of 12.5% of face value, i.e. Rs 1.25 per equity share for the year under review, subject to shareholders' approval.
The Company will be completing its first oil & gas O&M contract at the Suvali facility for Vedanta Resources in Q2 2026-27.
Complete the merger of Oilmax Energy Private Limited with Asian Energy Services Limited by September or October 2026.
The merger of Oilmax Energy Private Limited with the Company is expected to be completed by September or October 2026, subject to regulatory clearances.
Management has indicated confidence in growing the standalone India services business by 30-40% in 2026-27 with improved margins.
Targeted revenue of USD 60-65 Million from Kuiper in 2026-27.
Field development plan under implementation at the Indrora block targeting block-level production of approximately 1,000 barrels of oil per day by 2026-27.

Key priorities for 2026-27 include continued integration and scale-up of Kuiper, completion of the proposed merger of OEPL, execution of the Vedanta and MCL Lakhanpur contracts, and ramp-up of production at Indrora and the newly discovered Mewad field.
Ramp Indrora block production to approximately 1,000 barrels of oil per day by 2026-27 under a field development plan currently being implemented.
Scale Kuiper Group's existing business from approximately USD 60-70 Million in revenue to approximately USD 100 Million by 2028-29.
Target production of approximately 10,000 barrels of oil per day from the upstream asset portfolio by 2029-30.
Ramp Oilmax's upstream production from current output of approximately 2,500 BOPD to approximately 10,000 BOPD by 2028-29/2029-30 post merger.
Target approximately 10,000 BOPD peak production from the Oilmax upstream asset portfolio by 2029-30, with production expected to peak by 2028-29/2029-30 from current producing reserves.
The Company indicates an order book execution run rate of Rs 40-50 Crores per month.
Management will continue to monitor developments in West Asia, given their bearing on the international business.
Execute the Lakhanpur coal handling plant project awarded by Mahanadi Coalfields Limited, the largest CHP contract in the Company's history, and the integrated field management contract with Vedanta.

currentContext.expansion: Asian Energy's expansion during 2025-26 was driven by acquisition and contract wins rather than by plant capex. The Company acquired a 100% equity stake in Kuiper Group, UAE, from Gulf Capital through its wholly owned subsidiary Asian Oilfield & Energy Services DMCC ('ADMCC') for a cash consideration of USD 9.25 Million, giving immediate access to energy markets across the Middle East and Southeast Asia; Kuiper Group consolidated into the Company's financials from September 01, 2025. In parallel, the Company announced the proposed merger of its parent Oilmax Energy Private Limited with itself, which shareholders approved at meetings held on June 11 and June 12, 2026 and which is expected to complete by September or October 2026 subject to regulatory clearances; the merger would add five oil & gas blocks including one CBM asset, approximately 70 Million barrels of hydrocarbon reserves and current production of about 2,500 BOPD targeted to reach about 10,000 BOPD by 2028-29/2029-30. On execution, the Company secured an integrated field management contract with Vedanta Resources and the Lakhanpur coal handling plant project from Mahanadi Coalfields Limited, the largest CHP contract in its history, alongside the Suvali O&M and Gevra CHP contracts. At its Indrora block in Gujarat the NM-01 well began producing approximately 100 barrels of oil per day, with a further well NM-02 under testing and a field development plan under implementation targeting block-level production of approximately 1,000 barrels of oil per day by 2026-27; a newly discovered Mewad field is also earmarked for ramp-up. The Company describes its model as asset-light, focused on technical expertise and end-to-end project execution with limited equipment ownership, and reported that there are no capital commitments as on the respective reporting periods.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity in seismic and integrated energy services
risks.note: The growing number of seismic and integrated energy services providers may affect the Company's ability to secure new contracts. The Company states it maintains a competitive edge through strategic pricing, long-term client relationships and a proven record of successful project delivery. (MD&A 'Principal Risks and Mitigation Measures' — this table was routed to the strategy_outlook bundle rather than to this risks bundle, but is from the same annual report.)

risks.risk: Environmental compliance exposure in coal operations
risks.note: Non-compliance with environmental standards could damage the Company's reputation and reduce long-term demand for coal, potentially leading to lower coal prices. The Company has implemented a comprehensive Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) policy integrating environmental safeguards across its coal operations. (MD&A 'Principal Risks and Mitigation Measures', routed to the strategy_outlook bundle.)

risks.risk: Geopolitical exposure in West Asia affecting the international business
risks.note: Management explicitly flags that developments in West Asia remain a key variable to monitor, given their bearing on crude and LNG prices, shipping costs and the broader operating environment for energy services companies with an international footprint. The escalation of conflict in early 2026 disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and drove Brent from around USD 61 per barrel to a peak near USD 118 per barrel. With the Kuiper acquisition, a material part of the business now sits in the Middle East. (MD&A, routed to the strategy_outlook bundle.)

risks.risk: Crude price volatility and structurally decelerating global oil demand
risks.note: Prices have remained volatile, and global oil demand growth continued its structural deceleration, rising just 0.7% in 2025, with the IEA projecting an outright decline in demand for 2026. Global energy investment is increasingly directed toward renewables, grids, storage and low-emissions technologies rather than oil, gas and coal, which bears on long-run demand for upstream services. (MD&A, routed to the strategy_outlook bundle.)

risks.risk: Execution and integration risk on transformative M&A
risks.note: The Company is simultaneously integrating the newly acquired Kuiper Group, consolidated only from September 01, 2025, and pursuing the merger of its parent Oilmax Energy Private Limited, which remains subject to NCLT Mumbai hearing and final disposal and to regulatory clearances. Expected synergies, margin expansion and the scale-up to approximately USD 100 Million of Kuiper revenue depend on integration proceeding as planned.

risks.risk: Customer and contract concentration in a project-driven order book
risks.note: Revenue visibility rests on a standalone order book of approximately Rs 1,750 Crores concentrated in a small number of large contracts, with counterparties including Vedanta, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited, ONGC and Oil India. The award, deferral or loss of any single large contract materially affects the growth path.

risks.risk: Project execution disruption from weather and site conditions
risks.note: Management notes that extended monsoon conditions affected execution across certain projects during the first half of the year, requiring the teams to respond with agility and discipline to maintain project momentum — an ongoing structural exposure for a site-based EPC and material-handling business.

risks.risk: Governance and regulatory compliance lapses flagged by the Secretarial Auditor
risks.note: The Secretarial Auditor noted three observations: an analyst-meet intimation given at short notice without the required explanation, XBRL intimations for the May 16, 2025 Board Meeting outcome and the statutory auditor appointment filed with delay, and a postal-ballot remote e-voting window kept open beyond thirty days. Management responded that these were inadvertent and gave assurances of future adherence. Separately, the statutory auditors changed during the year, with Walker Chandiok & Co. resigning on completion of their second term and SGCO & Co. LLP appointed in their place.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Asian Energy Services Limited is an integrated energy and minerals services company with over three decades of experience across the upstream oil & gas and mining value chains.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Asian Energy is a service provider to the energy and mineral sectors offering end-to-end services across the value chain, including seismic surveys and geophysical data acquisition, integrated field development, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC), operations and maintenance (O&M) and enhanced oil recovery. The business is anchored in two complementary verticals: Integrated Oil & Gas Services, which supports upstream clients through the asset lifecycle, and Mineral Services, which delivers coal handling plants, bulk material handling systems and related engineering and execution solutions. Following the acquisition of Kuiper Group, the Company also provides integrated human resources, technical staffing and recruitment solutions to the energy industry internationally.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's energy security agenda, targeting a USD 100 Billion commitment to oil & gas investment by 2030, is expected to continue driving exploration and production activity, field redevelopment and integrated outsourcing of upstream operations
- Continued government focus on scientific exploration under HELP, OALP and DSF frameworks is expected to sustain demand for seismic and allied services
- The coal sector's production targets and asset monetization plans point to continued mineral infrastructure and material handling opportunities
- Growing industry preference for integrated field development models, which management believes will increasingly become the preferred operating model for upstream companies seeking greater productivity, operational efficiency and optimized lifecycle costs
- Long-term O&M contracts provide stable revenues, enhance earnings visibility and strengthen customer relationships
- India's hydrocarbon consumption continued to expand, with crude oil demand projected close to 6 Million barrels per day for 2026, while domestic crude production remained broadly range-bound, keeping import dependency elevated
- The Union Budget for 2026-27 allocated Rs 30,443 Crores to the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas and raised overall capital expenditure to Rs 12.2 Lakh Crores, or 4.4% of GDP, its highest share in a decade
- Domestic coal production is on track to approach a record 1.15 Billion tonnes in 2025-26 with the government targeting 1.31 Billion tonnes for 2026-27, alongside a coal asset monetization target of Rs 35,000 Crores
- Developments in West Asia remain a key variable to monitor, given their bearing on crude and LNG prices, shipping costs and the broader operating environment for energy services companies with an international footprint
- Kuiper integration is expected to unlock meaningful operational synergies, with margin upside from synergies, efficiencies and a shift to higher-value technical services
- The proposed Oilmax merger is expected to strengthen the balance sheet, improve capital allocation, enhance operational efficiency and create a more diversified business with balanced recurring and project-based revenue streams
- The Reserve Bank of India has projected growth of 6.6% for 2026-27, with inflation expected to firm to around 5.1% amid continuing global uncertainty, crude price volatility and currency pressures
- The Company's standalone order book stood at approximately Rs 1,750 Crores as of March 31, 2026, with a split of approximately 68% coming from oil & gas services verticals and approximately 32% from mineral services, providing revenue visibility for the coming years
- Integrated Oil & Gas Services formed around 68% of the total order book of approximately Rs 1,750 Crores, providing strong multi-year revenue visibility
- Mineral Services represented approximately 32% of the order book, equivalent to over Rs 566 Crores, providing a strong platform for future growth
- The Company secured two substantial new contracts during the year: an integrated field management contract with Vedanta Resources, and the Lakhanpur coal handling plant project awarded by Mahanadi Coalfields Limited, the largest CHP contract in the Company's history
- The Company submitted bids for three contract areas under Discovered Small Field Bid Round-4, and has been placed L1 in one additional coal handling plant tender
- The Kuiper acquisition provides revenue visibility of approximately USD 60-65 Million per annum through existing contracts and master service agreements
- A large bid pipeline in the services business provides a strong base for the next 2-3 years

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.
